dedupe_keys.name: usgs dam impact and disturbance metrics for the conterminous united states 1800 2018

description: This USGS data release gives two measures of how much reservoir storage affects every stream segment of the NHDPlus version 2 network in the conterminous United States, computed every ten years from 1800 to 2015. The first expresses upstream storage in days of mean annual flow, showing how long storage alone could sustain flow and hence the effect on average and low flows; the second is a dimensionless degree of regulation relative to 30-year average precipitation and upstream areas, aimed at peak flows. Storage, construction date and location come from the 2018 National Inventory of Dams, and the release includes those dam locations addressed to NHDPlusV2. The US Geological Survey produced and published it on ScienceBase in January 2021 as zipped files of about 200 to 230 MB with metadata, a free public-domain download. Coverage is national. Caveats: the metrics use maximum NID storage and so may overstate real reservoir impacts. Simulation uses: flagging regulated reaches in river network models and in flood and drought hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies. Related records: the National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) and HydroConDams (data-hydrocondams-hydrologically-consistent-dams).
